translation: Target defines the proposition asserting that for every set of arithmetic sentences K and every arithmetic theory (set of arithmetic sentences) F, assuming that F is recursively enumerable and that every theorem of 𝗜𝚺₁ (basic arithmetic with induction for Σ₁ formulas) is a theorem of F, if K (viewed as an arithmetic theory) is consistent (i.e., does not derive a contradiction in classical first-order logic), then it is not the case that both (1) K equals the set of all theorems of F ({σ | F ⊢ σ}) and (2) the consistency sentence ¬Prov_{F.craig}(⌜⊥⌝)—built from the standard provability predicate of the Δ₁-presented axiom set F.craig obtained from F via Craig's trick—belongs to K. Note that K is only required to be consistent (not true in the standard model ℕ), F is only required to be recursively enumerable and to contain all theorems of 𝗜𝚺₁ (not separately required to be consistent or Δ₁-presented), and the consistency sentence in (2) is specifically the one constructed from F.craig.

divergences.description: Soundness/correctness is replaced by consistency: both [P-K359] ('works correctly', ¬K(F_e ⊆ T)) and [P-K356] ('if K(F ⊆ T) then F ⊊ K', 'knowably sound algorithm') state their core claims in terms of knowing soundness/correctness, mentioning consistency in [P-K356] only as a minimal part of determining correctness. Because first-order arithmetic cannot express global soundness F ⊆ T as a single sentence, Target uses Def7 F ∈ K (a consistency sentence); for the impossibility claim under K = F this is a strengthening (assuming K recognizes that soundness implies consistency), though it shifts the predicate from soundness to consistency.

Omission of the epistemic self-identification disjunct ¬K(K = F_e) and epistemic modality: [P-K359] states a disjunction under K = F_e ('either we do not know the exact specification of the computer [¬K(K = F_e)] or we do not know that it works correctly [¬K(F_e ⊆ T)]'). Because K is formalized simply as a Set ArithmeticSentence with no epistemic operator or self-reference to K, Lean cannot express K(K = F_e) or K(F_e ⊆ T), and Target drops the ¬K(K = F_e) disjunct altogether—strengthening the conclusion logically while losing the epistemic distinction in [P-K359].

Mere non-equality (K ≠ F.theory) instead of strict inclusion (F ⊊ K), and no ruling out of refuting consistency: relative to [P-K356]'s 'if K(F ⊆ T) then F ⊊ K', Target only yields Def7 F ∈ K → K ≠ F.theory (under Def4 K), omitting F.theory ⊆ K because knowing consistency alone does not entail containing all theorems of F. Likewise, relative to [P-K356]'s closing remark on determining ('absolutely prove or refute') whether F is consistent, Target only rules out proving consistency (Def7 F ∈ K), not refuting it (∼(Def7 F) ∈ K), which remains compatible with a merely consistent K equal to F.theory.

Extensional RE set with a single noncomputable Craig presentation (F.craig) rather than a given machine/presentation F_e: both the author's claim ('a given machine ... know that machine to be consistent') and [P-K359] (F_e, 'exact specification of the computer') refer to an intensional machine/specification. Target instead quantifies over extensional axiom sets F with proof-irrelevant [F.RE] and defines Def7 F via F.craig.consistent.val (one unspecified, classically chosen Craig-tricked Δ₁ presentation of F), rather than quantifying over machine codes or arbitrary Δ₁ presentations [F.Δ₁]. Because different RE enumerations of the same axiom set F can produce non-equivalent consistency sentences, Target strictly only rules out membership of that single Craig-tricked consistency sentence.

Added arithmetical strength assumption [𝗜𝚺₁ ⪯ F]: Target explicitly requires F to contain all theorems of IΣ₁. This hypothesis is not stated explicitly in [P-K359] or [P-K356], though it is a standard implicit prerequisite for Gödel's second incompleteness theorem.

Restriction to first-order arithmetic and weakening of soundness to consistency of K: the passages refer to human mathematical intuition/knowledge (factive/sound and not limited to arithmetic), whereas Target idealizes K as a set of first-order arithmetic sentences (Set ArithmeticSentence) and assumes only syntactic consistency (Def4 K) rather than soundness (Def3 K)—a standard idealization and, for ruling out Def7 F ∈ K, a harmless strengthening.

Omission of the non-refutation claim in [P-K359]: Target formalizes only the impossibility conditional and does not capture the opening remark of [P-K359] that the incompleteness results do not rule out K = F_e (consistent with the author's narrower claim).

judgement.summary: Target accurately formalizes the Gödelian consistency-level anti-conjunction claim via Gödel's second incompleteness theorem—a consistent mind K cannot both equal F.theory and contain F's consistency sentence—with only minor caveats relative to the claim and source passages. The main caveats are the shift from the passages' soundness/epistemic claims (K(F ⊆ T), ¬K(K = F_e), F ⊊ K, and proving/refuting consistency) to a purely arithmetical consistency statement, the explicit [𝗜𝚺₁ ⪯ F] strength hypothesis, and the use of a single noncomputably chosen Craig presentation F.craig for extensional RE theories rather than quantifying over given machine specifications/presentations.
